newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Put buyers in Gateway.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Put buyers in Gateway.

text.p: Put buyers in Gateway 2000 Inc were out in force Wednesday as the stock fell sharply, option traders said.d
Gateway was down 1-3/4 at 60-1/4 in early afternoon on more than 3.7 million shares. Just last week the stock was trading near its all-time highs above 74.
"There's a lot of bearish order flow," one market maker in the options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange said. "There are a lot of in-the-money put buyers."
Gateway options trade on the CBOE, the American Stock Exchange and the Pacific Exchange. Most orders Wednesday crossed at the CBOE.
The market maker said the big trade was a put butterfly in the June 55, 65 and 75 options, done on a two by four by two basis.
Butterfly spreads are typically used to bet on volatility. Traders said volatility in Gateway has been climbing as the stock dropped sharply over the last week.
"Volatility continues to expand," the market maker said. Implied volatility for Gateway June options was around 80.
The June 55 puts traded a total of 2,475 contracts by early afternoon, the June 65s traded about 4,350 and the June 75s traded 2,000.
The market maker said the investor sold the 55s and 75s and bought the 65s.

Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at Everen Securities, said Gateway shares have quickly approached "significant intermediate" support in the low-60 to upper-50 region, and whether they hold will be key for the stock's direction.
"Short term, the trend is deteriorating. Intermediate to long term the trend remains positive," he said.
If the stock is able to hold current support levels and then rebound back over the 65-66 zone, it could recover back to test its 75-3/8 record high, reached on May 21 and tested on May 28, Nie said.
Gateway shares are set to split two-for-one on June 16.
